clue.text: Close to centre, from memory

parts.note: by means near or close to, as in 'stand by the door'
the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: Someone describing a spot near the middle, recalled without notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something this way is to have memorised it, recalling it without written help.

clue.text: Large amount in pails

definitions.meaning: as in it rained by the bucketload, lots

explanation.surface: Plenty of something carried in buckets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pails and, informally, a great quantity, as in crying copious tears.

clue.text: Play organ before holiday audience

parts.note: the heart is an organ of the body
a break is a short holiday
a theatre audience is called the house, as in a full house

explanation.surface: Performing on the organ in front of holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a George Bernard Shaw drama first staged in 1920.

clue.text: Scoffed about a new tray, new if nothing else

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for scoffed goes round the rest

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed is ate
taken as written

indicators.note: new means a fresh version, so the letters of tray are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ate around a fresh tray, which is at least something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' does two jobs: once as the abbreviation N, once as the anagram signal for tray; 'about' puts that group inside the word for scoffed, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in any case or at least, conceding a minimum.

clue.text: Symbol, from time to time, put up

indicators.note: put up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sign that's hoisted now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to letters taken from 'time to time', and in a down clue 'put up' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved pole or emblem represents a clan, serving as its symbol.

clue.text: An object enthralling male in a Disney location

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the word for object holds the male inside it

parts.note: an aim is an object or goal
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A captivating thing holding a man spellbound at a Disney site.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian city is home to Disneyland, the original Disney theme park resort.

clue.text: Football team in Scotland are untidy, in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means in a muddle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Scottish side whose players are scruffy and disorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: This club plays at Somerset Park in the Ayrshire coastal town.

clue.text: Cause anger blowing top in joint

indicators.note: blowing one's top is losing one's temper; here the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to rankle is to cause lasting anger

explanation.surface: Something infuriating, flying off the handle at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's link between foot and leg is a hinge joint.

clue.text: Informal alliance Alec entered into unwisely

indicators.note: doing something unwisely suggests it is muddled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Alec rashly signed up to a pact.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1904 Anglo-French understanding was a friendly agreement rather than a formal treaty.

clue.text: Mother holding headgear for religious sage

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the word for mother wraps round headgear

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A mother clutching a hat meant for a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: The title means great soul in Sanskrit and is given to revered teachers, like Gandhi.

clue.text: Vignette of eccentric with small sailing boat

parts.note: an eccentric person is called a character
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A short portrait of an oddball who owns a little yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a brief descriptive piece, just like a short portrait of one person in words.

clue.text: List of competitors in lobby

definitions.meaning: the field of those entered for a race or contest
a hallway or vestibule by which one goes in

explanation.surface: Where the roster of contestants is posted, in the hall.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the roll of entrants in a contest; the other is a doorway hall, both common senses.

clue.text: Scamp with fruitcake, and something else to eat

parts.note: a cheeky child or scamp is called a little monkey
a fruitcake, slang for a crazy person, is also a nut

explanation.surface: A rascal with a slice of fruitcake, plus another snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitcake' pretends to be food, which makes 'something else to eat' read naturally, but it means a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the peanut, an edible snack, hence food beyond the cake.

clue.text: Cover a wider area — might that be suggested by padres?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: put the letters of the first word out of order, and they make padres

explanation.surface: Asking whether chaplains hint at expanding coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' works as an anagram signal applied to the first word, and the result is the word padres in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend over a larger area is to stretch or fan across more ground.

clue.text: Recovering, continuously injecting them

indicators.note: injecting means putting inside, so them goes into the phrase for continuously

parts.note: on end is a phrase meaning nonstop, as in for hours on end

explanation.surface: Getting better after a constant course of shots.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means improving in health after illness or injury.

clue.text: Theatre scene

definitions.meaning: a theatre of operations or performance space
the scene or sphere of activity, as in the political stage

explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a place of action or contest, like a stadium or sphere of conflict.

clue.text: High priest's staff producing novel

definitions.meaning: the miraculous budding staff of the Hebrew high priest in Exodus
a 1922 novel by D. H. Lawrence

explanation.surface: A clergyman's crook that inspires a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical staff of Moses' brother and the D. H. Lawrence novel share this name.

clue.text: Conscious of a conflict close to home

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here of home

explanation.surface: Knowing that fighting is near one's own doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert to something means knowing about it or being mindful of it.

clue.text: Inflexible, a guy surrounded by detailed facts and figures

indicators.note: surrounded by means the man goes inside the word for facts and figures
de-tailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: data are facts and figures
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A rigid fellow buried in exhaustive statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed: DATA loses its final A to give DAT, which surrounds MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unyielding refuses to change their mind, utterly firm.

clue.text: Emblem in house, mounted

parts.note: the Tudors were a royal house of England
rose, past tense of rise, means climbed or mounted

explanation.surface: A crest fixed up high in a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' here is a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-and-white flower badge is the heraldic symbol of England since Henry VII.

clue.text: Intensely serious article penned by Hemingway, perhaps

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the article sits inside the name

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway, the American author, is an example of the forename
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grave piece of writing by the author of The Old Man and the Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' suggests writing, but here it means shut in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sincere and solemn in manner is being intensely serious.

clue.text: Result of bumpkin being caught by a belt?

definitions.text: Result of bumpkin being caught by a belt?

indicators.note: being caught by puts the bumpkin inside the word for belt

parts.note: to belt is to race along, to tear
a hick is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A yokel hit by a blow ends up with a swollen ear.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, a belt is a punch; as wordplay, belt means to rush. 'Result of' is a link in the wordplay reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen ear is the familiar British phrase for the outcome of a cuff round the head.

clue.text: Cardinal, say, breaking firm set of beliefs

indicators.note: breaking into means getting inside, so the colour goes into the firm

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
cardinal is a shade of red, so red is an example

explanation.surface: A churchman bursting into a company's statement of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a prelate; here it is the bright red colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a statement of principles or religious faith.

clue.text: Proportion of allowance reduced

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A share of a smaller allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts the final N from RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation between two quantities, as in three to one, is a proportion.

clue.text: Floor of drain in need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so the letters of drain are rearranged

explanation.surface: The bottom of a broken drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point, figuratively the rock bottom or floor of something.

clue.text: Where bandits are likely to take your money?

definitions.text: Where bandits are likely to take your money?

parts.words: Where bandits are likely to take your money?
parts.note: bandits suggests robbers, but one-armed bandits are slot machines found at a seaside games hall

explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine; British seaside gaming halls are full of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slot machines, nicknamed one-armed bandits, take coins in such a gaming venue.

clue.text: What climber may need to carry crossing face of Eiger

indicators.note: the phrase to carry straddles the letter, going across it on both sides

parts.note: taken as written
to hold is to carry

indicators.note: the face of a word is its first letter, here of Eiger

explanation.surface: Equipment a mountaineer might bring when traversing the Eiger's north face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry' suggests lugging gear up the mountain, but the clue is a container: 'crossing' has the two-word phrase straddle the Eiger's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny ledge where a boot tip can rest is what a rock climber needs for purchase.

clue.text: Irregular soldiers tense? A bit

parts.note: odd means irregular or unmatched
men is a common word for soldiers
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Irregular troops a little edgy.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap or remnant is a bit or piece.
